coverage_note: Roughly 14:53-20:30 is an all-English planning talk (AI tools, tests); 12:27-13:25, 20:31-30:23, 36:37-42:59 and 45:18-1:00:46 are Latin-transliterated, often garbled (e.g. 25:05-25:38 'ana bihna binkhales al-asal', 'ahana shay na'na' ma asal mufrad' could not be parsed into rows). 22:49-24:55 is a honey seller at the door (not Amal). Speaker labels are fragmented; many '?' lines were assigned from flow (e.g. 02:31 'or يتعلّم', 34:00 'هو بتيبست' self-fixed). The lesson is one long drill on بسّط/انبسط conjugations, so grammar rows dominate and vocab rows are few. Left out as S4 pronunciation: لقة/luka for لغة (00:39), بسّتني for بسطني (30:35), بيسبت for بيبسط (32:30), بنسبت for بنبسط (34:21), bansebet for banbeset (56:04), بيسبط for ببسّط (1:02:23), maruj for mahruj (22:09), 'ma' for ma3 (25:38, 26:19), stress on the T (55:25). Self-fixes not logged: أكتب→احكي (05:28), سميح→مبسوط (27:54), basati→basatini (41:09), بساتِتني→بساتِتك (35:58). English words inside Arabic not on her sheet, so not tier 3: software, research, possibility, test (she uses 'test' herself), mispronounce, AI. 26:19 'aswad' read as aswa2 = worse (on sheet), so not a vocab error.
